study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative trajectories of R 1 , R 2 *, and magnetic susceptibility in basal ganglia on healthy ageing

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives and the purpose of using normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Our objectives were threefold: (1) to delineate normative trajectories across subcortical grey matter nuclei throughout the lifespan...; (2) to investigate the independence of deviations...; (3) to examine the independence of variations... Lastly, we tested the utility of the normative trajectories in a validation dataset... Gaining insights into how these quantitative measurements evolve throughout a normal lifespan can enhance our understanding of brain maturation processes and facilitate studies of disease- related microstructural changes

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses the ABRIM dataset. Eligibility criteria, image quality standards (visual assessment by three raters), and exclusion reasons/final sample size are described.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Data utilised to derive the normative trajectories is part of the Advanced Brain Imaging on Ageing and Memory (ABRIM) data collection... Three raters (M.J., K.C., and M.R.) visually assessed the quality of all datasets. The following criteria were used to exclude data... Forty- one participants were excluded... resulting in data of 260 participants

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex, Hemisphere) are included in the GLM and GPR models. It is a single-site study (ABRIM) so site effects are not applicable, but harmonized protocol is mentioned.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: The design matrix comprised four regressors: Age, Age 2 , Sex, and (left- / right- ) Hemisphere... In the following normative modelling analysis, the data were corrected for the sex- specific and inter- hemispherical effects based on the GLM results.
